title: Valid Palindrome With One Deletion
statement:
Decide whether a lowercase string can become a palindrome after removing at most one character.

Contract
- `text` is non-null and may be empty. Every character is a lowercase English letter (`a` through `z`).
- Removing zero characters is allowed, so strings that are already palindromes return `true`.
- Removing at most one character at any index is allowed; you may not reorder or replace characters.
- Return `true` when zero or one deletion produces a string that reads the same forward and backward, and `false` otherwise.

Examples
- `canBePalindrome("aba")` returns `true` (already a palindrome).
- `canBePalindrome("abca")` returns `true` (delete `'b'` or `'c'`).
- `canBePalindrome("abc")` returns `false`.
hints: Walk two indexes inward from the ends while the characters match; the matched outer prefix and suffix never need to be deleted.
At the first mismatch `text.charAt(left) != text.charAt(right)`, one of those two characters must be the single deleted character.
Check whether either substring `(left + 1 .. right)` or `(left .. right - 1)` is a strict palindrome using a helper loop. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
inputSyntax: Input: a lowercase word between single quotes, for example: 'abca'
